title: The Golem's Eye
author: Jonathan Stroud
summary: Bartimaeus Sequence, book 2. A section-by-section title following Bartimaeus, Nathaniel and Kitty as a clay golem terrorizes London. Pass each story section as you read, then sit the whole-book test at the end.

questions.q: Where does the book's opening scene take place?
questions.why: The prologue goes back in time to Prague, long before the main story.

questions.q: Who is Bartimaeus serving in the opening scene?
questions.why: Bartimaeus is working for a magician of Prague when the city is attacked.

questions.q: Which army is attacking Prague in the prologue?
options: A British army led by Gladstone
questions.why: Gladstone's British forces are storming the city, which shows how Britain's magicians built their empire.

questions.q: What happens to Bartimaeus's master during the attack?
questions.why: His master dies, which frees Bartimaeus from that service.

questions.q: Why does the story start with a scene set so long before Nathaniel's time?
options: To explain how Nathaniel got his name
To show the history behind Britain's power and Prague's magic
It has no connection to the rest of the book
questions.why: Prague and Gladstone both matter later: the golem comes from Prague's magic, and Gladstone's tomb is a key location.

questions.q: About how old is Nathaniel at the start of the main story?
questions.why: The book picks up a couple of years after The Amulet of Samarkand, with Nathaniel at fourteen.

questions.q: What name does Nathaniel use in public as a magician?
questions.why: Magicians hide their birth names, so Nathaniel works as John Mandrake.

questions.q: Which magician is Nathaniel's mentor and master in this book?
questions.why: Jessica Whitwell, the Minister of Security, has taken him under her wing.

questions.q: Who is Nathaniel's boss at the Ministry of Internal Affairs?
questions.why: Nathaniel works under Tallow, who resents his talented young assistant.

questions.q: What task has Nathaniel been given that he is struggling to complete?
questions.why: His career depends on stopping the commoner Resistance, and his lack of progress makes him look bad.

questions.q: What game are Kitty and Jakob playing when their trouble with magicians begins?
questions.why: A cricket ball from their game hits a magician's car.

questions.q: Whose car is hit by the ball?
questions.why: The car belongs to Julius Tallow, who takes cruel revenge.

questions.q: What curse does Tallow's djinni use on the children?
questions.why: The Black Tumbler is the curse that falls on Kitty and Jakob.

questions.q: What is surprising about how the curse affects Kitty?
options: It doesn't hurt her, while Jakob is badly harmed
It hurts her but not Jakob
questions.why: Kitty is resistant to magic, and this unusual gift shapes the rest of her story.

questions.q: What happens when Kitty takes Tallow to court?
questions.why: The court sides with the magician, a clear example of how unfair the system is to commoners.

questions.q: Who pays Kitty's fine after the court case?
questions.why: Mr. Pennyfeather covers the fine and then invites her into his group.

questions.q: What is the Resistance trying to do?
options: Fight back against the magicians' power
questions.why: The Resistance is a small group of commoners working against the magicians who govern Britain.

questions.q: Why is Kitty especially valuable to the Resistance?
questions.why: Magic that would harm others has little effect on her, which makes her useful on dangerous missions.

questions.q: Which of these people is a member of Kitty's Resistance group?
questions.why: Stanley, Fred, Anne and Nick are among Kitty's fellow Resistance members.

questions.q: What role does Mr. Hopkins play for the Resistance?
options: He is a scholar who passes them information
He is their leader in battle
questions.why: Hopkins brings the group information, including where to find valuable magical objects.

questions.q: Where does the first mysterious attack happen?
options: Pinn's Accoutrements, a shop in Piccadilly
questions.why: The first attack destroys Sholto Pinn's shop.

questions.q: On what special day does the Piccadilly attack happen?
questions.why: The attack happens during the Founder's Day celebrations.

questions.q: Who does the government blame for the attacks?
questions.why: The newspapers and officials blame the Resistance, even though the truth is very different.

questions.q: Why does Nathaniel summon Bartimaeus again?
options: Ms. Whitwell orders him to send Bartimaeus home
He needs a powerful, clever servant to help solve the attacks
He wants to learn Bartimaeus's history
questions.why: Under pressure to get results, Nathaniel calls up the djinni who helped him before.

questions.q: What does Bartimaeus eventually figure out about the attacker?
questions.why: After fighting it, Bartimaeus identifies the creature as a golem, a clay giant that magic can hardly touch.

questions.q: Where is Gladstone buried?
questions.why: The Resistance breaks into Gladstone's tomb in Westminster Abbey.

questions.q: Why does the Resistance break into the tomb?
options: To hide from the Night Police
questions.why: Their information says the tomb holds magical treasures they could use against the magicians.

questions.q: What guards Gladstone's remains?
options: The afrit Honorius, bound into his bones
questions.why: Honorius was bound to Gladstone's bones and rises when the tomb is opened.

questions.q: What object does Kitty escape with?
questions.why: Kitty gets away with Gladstone's staff, which becomes very important later.

questions.q: What is the result of the raid for the Resistance?
options: Most of the group is killed
questions.why: Honorius kills Pennyfeather and several others, which destroys the group. The raid shows the heavy cost of meddling with old magic.

questions.q: Why do Nathaniel and Bartimaeus go to Prague?
options: To find out who made the golem
questions.why: Golems are a Prague magic, so the trail of the attacks leads there.

questions.q: Who is the British spy they meet in Prague?
questions.why: Harlequin, a British agent working undercover, helps them in Prague.

questions.q: Who is Kavka?
options: The Prague magician who made the golem's parchment
questions.why: Kavka made the parchment that brings the golem to life.

questions.q: Why did Kavka help create the golem?
options: He was paid by the Resistance
questions.why: A British traitor blackmailed him into making it.

questions.q: What happens to the parchment evidence in Prague?
options: It is sent to the Prime Minister
It is framed in a museum
questions.why: The evidence that might have exposed the traitor is lost, so Nathaniel returns without proof.

questions.q: How does Julius Tallow die?
options: Being hit by a cricket ball
In the raid on Gladstone's tomb
Summoning a spirit from books that had been secretly altered
In a golem attack at Piccadilly
questions.why: The Hyrnek family, who print magicians' books, had secretly altered his, and his summoning goes wrong.

questions.q: Why is the Hyrnek family's secret act important?
options: It shows commoners finding quiet ways to strike back
questions.why: Jakob's family got back at Tallow without open rebellion.

questions.q: Who is in charge of the Night Police?
questions.why: Police chief Duvall commands the Night Police and uses the crisis to gain power.

questions.q: What are the Night Police?
questions.why: Duvall's Night Police are werewolves, which makes them frightening enforcers.

questions.q: How does Nathaniel try to find Kitty?
options: He uses Jakob to lure her
questions.why: Nathaniel uses Kitty's friend Jakob as bait, a sign of how ruthless he is becoming.

questions.q: Who rescues Kitty from the Night Police?
questions.why: Bartimaeus saves Kitty, which leads to an unexpected conversation between them.

questions.q: Whose form does Bartimaeus take when he talks with Kitty?
questions.why: He appears as Ptolemy, a past master he remembers with respect.

questions.q: What does Bartimaeus talk to Kitty about?
options: The rise and fall of empires
questions.why: He explains that empires rise and fall and that magicians' power doesn't last forever.

questions.q: Why is the conversation important for Kitty?
options: It teaches her the Black Tumbler
It helps her see her struggle as part of history
It convinces her to join the government
questions.why: Bartimaeus's view of history gives her a bigger picture of what the magicians' rule really is.

questions.q: What does this section show about Bartimaeus?
options: Under the jokes he thinks deeply about humans and power
questions.why: The sarcastic djinni shows serious, thoughtful knowledge from thousands of years of service.

questions.q: What destroys Honorius?
questions.why: In the climax, the golem destroys the afrit Honorius.

questions.q: How does Kitty stop the golem?
options: She pulls the parchment from its mouth
She throws it into the Thames
questions.why: The parchment in its mouth brings it to life; without it, the golem stops.

questions.q: Where does the crumbling golem go after it is stopped?
options: Back to its master, Henry Duvall
questions.why: It returns to its controller, revealing Duvall as the traitor.

questions.q: What does Bartimaeus tell Nathaniel about Kitty?
options: That she was destroyed, though it isn't true
That she stole the staff again
questions.why: Bartimaeus lies to protect Kitty, who survives and stays in London to study magic's history.

questions.q: By the end, what does Bartimaeus calling Nathaniel 'John Mandrake' suggest?
options: Nathaniel has become more like the ruthless magicians around him
questions.why: Nathaniel is promoted, but the djinni's words show he is losing the boy he used to be.

verdicts.high: Even Bartimaeus would be impressed. Brilliant reading!
verdicts.pass: Well done. On to the next section.
verdicts.fail: Below the passing mark. Read it again and come back.

questions.q: Who are the three main narrators or viewpoint characters?
questions.why: Chapters switch between the djinni, the young magician and the commoner.

questions.q: How are Bartimaeus's chapters different from the others?
options: They are told in first person with funny footnotes
questions.why: Bartimaeus narrates his own chapters and adds witty footnotes.

questions.q: What brings the golem to life?
options: A parchment placed in its mouth
questions.why: Removing that parchment is how Kitty stops it.

questions.q: Who secretly controls the golem?
questions.why: The golem returning to Duvall reveals him as the man behind it.

questions.q: What special trait does Kitty have?
options: She can see through the golem's eye
questions.why: Her resilience protects her in dangerous scenes.

questions.q: Who is Jakob Hyrnek to Kitty?
questions.why: Jakob's injury from the Black Tumbler starts Kitty's fight against the magicians.

questions.q: Which afrit is freed from Gladstone's tomb?
questions.why: Honorius was bound into Gladstone's bones.

questions.q: Where do the golem's attacks happen?
options: Pinn's shop, the National Gallery and the British Museum
questions.why: The golem strikes several London sites while the Resistance is blamed.

questions.q: Why is the Resistance blamed for the golem's attacks?
options: It is a convenient scapegoat for powerful magicians
questions.why: Blaming commoners hides the traitor inside the government.

questions.q: What happens to Queezle?
options: She is killed by the golem
questions.why: Bartimaeus's fellow spirit Queezle dies in a golem attack.

questions.q: What position does Nathaniel win at the end?
questions.why: Stopping the crisis gets him promoted.

questions.q: What does Kitty decide to do at the end?
options: Stay in London and study the history of magic
questions.why: She survives and sets out to understand magic's past.

questions.q: What happens to Jakob at the end?
options: He leaves for Bruges with forged papers
questions.why: His family helps him get away safely.

questions.q: Which statement best describes how Nathaniel changes in this book?
options: He grows more ambitious and ruthless
questions.why: Using Jakob as bait and chasing promotion show him hardening.

questions.q: What big idea does the book explore through the magicians and commoners?
options: How power can be unfair and corrupt
questions.why: The unfair court case, the blame game and Duvall's plot show power being abused.

questions.q: How is Nathaniel different from Kitty?
options: He works inside the system; she fights against it
questions.why: Their opposite sides drive much of the book's tension.

questions.q: What is Gladstone's importance in this world?
options: He is the founder of magicians' rule in Britain
questions.why: Founder's Day honors him, and his tomb holds powerful treasures.

questions.q: Why is a golem such a dangerous enemy for magicians and spirits?
options: Magic has little effect on it
questions.why: Spirits like Queezle can't stand against it, which makes the attacks so frightening.

questions.q: What is Nemaides?
options: Tallow's djinni who carries out the Black Tumbler
questions.why: Tallow's servant delivered the curse that hurt Jakob.

questions.q: What does the book suggest about Bartimaeus's view of human empires?
options: They all rise and eventually fall
questions.why: His history lesson to Kitty shows he has seen many empires come and go.
